knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A written, itemised scope with exclusions, priced under the approved method, lets the client see what is included and keeps the price defensible.
Selling animals or chemical treatments as add-ons is outside this kind of service. A test report, a materials-charged media refresh and a review date are all within scope.
Referral arrangements must be checked against the rules for fees, advertising and inducements, and disclosed to the client before they are used.

practicalCriteria: Learner writes a scope with tiers, exclusions and a price basis for a training aquarium maintenance offer
Learner identifies the disclosure step required before a referral fee arrangement is used, and states it in writing
Learner declines to sell an animal or treatment as an add-on in a role-play, and records the reason
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Written service scope with tiers, exclusions and price basis
Disclosure note for the referral arrangement
Refusal record for the add-on request
Assessor review of the scope against the licence notices
stopWorkCriteria: An offer that includes electrical, plumbing or animal treatment work the business is not authorised to do
A referral fee accepted without disclosure to the client
A promise of an outcome for the animals
